pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we develop a good narrative?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension
2. write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication
3. appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition to a partner. (skill: write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate creativity and good handwriting in effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we develop a good narrative?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Narrative composition means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify elements of a narrative composition for comprehension.
5. Be able to: write texts based on the theme using good handwriting for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
